findings.description: A Dependabot head update between required-check polling and auto-merge enablement may be merged without checks for the new head.
findings.analysis: The proposed race is a small timing window in a single-user repository. It is not material enough to justify additional workflow complexity.
findings.rationale: The repository's single-user operating model makes this theoretical window immaterial.

findings.description: A file replacement between pathname type check and read may allow a special file to block validation.
findings.analysis: Exploitation requires a concurrent local writer replacing a validation input after the type check. This does not match the repository's practical validation threat model.
findings.rationale: Disproportionate hardening for an inapplicable concurrent local attack.

findings.description: A non-regular installed SKILL.md can be skipped before the regular-file reader reports it.
findings.analysis: A genuinely absent SKILL.md remains a valid unmarked user/client directory. A present or broken-link SKILL.md that fails the regular-file check must instead produce a path-specific validation diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: Branch on absent versus non-regular candidate SKILL.md files and fail validation for the latter.
findings.rationale: Validation must surface a non-regular candidate file without imposing requirements on directories that contain no skill file.

dispatch.outcome: Installed-skill discovery now fails for existing or broken-link non-regular SKILL.md candidates while directories with no SKILL.md remain ignored.

findings.description: A filesystem error from Path.exists() could make an unreadable selector look absent.
findings.analysis: The selector is optional and local. Distinguishing every platform-specific lookup failure from absence adds defensive complexity without a material repository risk.
findings.rationale: Disproportionate handling for a hypothetical failure of an optional local file.

findings.description: The ordinary token may lack permissions for default Dependabot alert or compatibility lookup.
findings.analysis: dependabot/fetch-metadata defaults alert-lookup and compat-lookup to false. Neither optional lookup is enabled, so the documented ordinary github.token path applies.
findings.rationale: The finding assumes default optional lookups that the action documentation states are disabled.

findings.description: The workflow-order test does not prove the App-token step retains its eligibility condition.
findings.analysis: GitHub workflow configuration is reviewed directly and is not production Python code. Workflow-specific tests are outside the repository's test policy.
findings.recommendation: Remove the workflow-specific test; inspect workflow semantics during review instead.
findings.rationale: Tests are reserved for production code, not declarative workflow configuration.

findings.description: The regular-status-symlink test does not prove runtime discovery loaded the linked record.
findings.analysis: The regression coverage is intentionally limited to non-regular-file detection. Symlink discovery behaviour is not the subject of this change.
findings.rationale: The proposed assertion tests behaviour outside the intended regression boundary.

findings.description: The workflow-order test does not bind ordinary-token assertions to the metadata and check-polling steps.
findings.analysis: The workflow-specific test has been removed under the cross-project policy that tests cover production code only.
findings.recommendation: Inspect declarative workflow semantics directly during review.
findings.rationale: Workflow configuration is not production code and is not covered by Python tests.
